extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: A benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning and natural language understanding, focusing on everyday situations with a preference for atypical solutions.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Annotators were prompted with links to instructables.com and asked to articulate a physical goal and a valid solution. They were also asked to provide a permutation to their own solution which makes it invalid.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was cleaned of basic artifacts using the AFLite algorithm, which discards instances whose given feature representations are collectively highly indicative of the target label to perform systematic data bias reduction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were seeded with instructables drawn from six categories. They articulated a goal and a valid solution, and provided a trick (an invalid solution). Data was collected in batches and validated by other annotators for correctness. Examples with low agreement were removed.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Data was validated by other annotators for correctness. Examples with low agreement were removed from the data, which often included correct examples requiring expert-level knowledge. Users with low agreement were de-qualed.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset addresses reporting bias in text (where commonsense properties are rarely reported). It also addresses stylistic annotation artifacts and trivial examples by using the AFLite algorithm for systematic data bias reduction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automated methods trained on large web crawls may eventually surpass human performance on this dataset, as human performance was calculated by a majority vote and some 'mistakes' are actually correct but required a web search to verify.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking progress in physical commonsense understanding, evaluating language representations on their knowledge of physical commonsense, and multiple choice question answering (Training, Development, and Testing).
